title: OpenTelemetry export translation bridge for vendor-agnostic trace handoff
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Build a lightweight translation bridge that accepts OpenTelemetry-formatted traces from our ingress, normalizes schema differences, and reliably forwards to a configurable set of vendor backends (e.g., Tempo-like and Jaeger-like endpoints) while preserving sampling decisions and trace context.

Scope:
- Input: OpenTelemetry ExportRequest (gRPC/HTTP).
- Output: Multiple backend formats via pluggable adapters (HTTP/GRPC/formatted envelopes).
- Behavior: preserve trace IDs/span relationships/timing; convert semantic attributes where backend expects different keys; attach tenant metadata; implement batching and backpressure to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Non-goals: this is not a full OTLP collector replacement (no metrics pipeline in this ticket), nor an ingestion catalog for legacy instrumentation (migration tasks will be separate).

Design notes:
- Adapter model: small adapter interface that implements transformEnvelope(spanList, tenantHint) -> encodedPayload + headers. New adapters can be added without restarting the bridge.
- Attribute mapping: maintain a mapping table and a fallback rule (snake_case -> camelCase if backend requires). Configurable per-tenant.
- Sampling and trace-context: preserve otel.trace_id and otel.span_id; translate trace-flags into backend sampling tags where applicable.
- Reliability: in-flight queue with per-tenant caps, retry policy with exponential backoff and jitter for 5xx/connection errors, configurable dead-lettering to S3 for persistent failures.
- Performance: batching should be size and time based (e.g., 1000 spans or 100ms) with dynamic tuning via observed per-backend latency.
- Security: TLS and optional mTLS to destination backends; credential rotation via secret manager.

Engineering trade-offs considered:
- Why not reuse full OpenTelemetry Collector? We need a footprint optimized for our tracing topology with per-tenant routing and Redwood-specific metadata enrichment. Reusing OT Collector would add a lot of unused components and complexity.
- In-process adapters vs worker model: chose separate adapter worker pool to avoid adapter-level CPU spikes impacting ingest path.

Rollout plan: Canary in us-west with a single non-production tenant, monitor success ratio and P95 export latency, then expand to low-volume customers, then GA behind feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge accepts OpenTelemetry ExportRequest over gRPC and HTTP and returns 200/OK for successfully queued batches
At least two adapters implemented: Jaeger-JSON-compatible envelope and Tempo-batch-compatible envelope
Sampling flags and trace IDs are preserved in the forwarded payloads and verified end-to-end via synthetic traces
Configurable per-tenant attribute mapping applies and falls back to default mapping when unset
Backpressure observed under high-latency backend and queue limits prevent OOM or unbounded memory growth
Automated e2e test suite validates translation correctness and retry semantics (CI job passing)
